answer: Submissions that land within 103 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The zenith detector writes to trellis, and sable shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 272 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 33 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
